- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or shows strong bearish signals, model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect risk-off sentiment.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots in next period; cap forecast at 1–2% below peak or use lagged mean.
- When sentiment flips from bullish to bearish (or vice versa), model lags by 1–3 days; adjust forecast to align with sentiment shift 1–2 days ahead.
- Model underperforms in early horizon (1–3 days) when sentiment is volatile; use 3-day moving average or sentiment-weighted median for short-term correction.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often overestimates mean price; apply 5–10% downward bias if sentiment is neutral or mixed.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 values (bearish), model tends to underestimate; add 2–5% upward bias to compensate for bearish bias.
- When sentiment is 1.00 for 3+ consecutive days, model overfits to recent highs; apply mean reversion to 10–15% of 30-day average.
